import os
import subprocess
import sys

from sase.vcs_provider import get_vcs_provider

checkout_target = {{ setup.checkout_target | tojson }}
project_name = {{ setup.project_name | tojson }}
gh_ref = {{ gh_ref | tojson }}

provider = get_vcs_provider(os.getcwd())

# Checkout the PR branch so that subsequent diffs are relative to the
# PR tip rather than the default branch. Try checkout_target first
# (works for default-branch refs like origin/main), then fall back to
# Patch name -> branch name conversion.
is_patch = checkout_target == f"origin/{gh_ref}"
ok, err = provider.checkout(checkout_target, os.getcwd())
if not ok:
    if is_patch:
        # Patch ref — resolve name to branch name
        resolved = provider.resolve_revision(
            gh_ref, project_name, os.getcwd()
        )
        ok, err = provider.checkout(resolved, os.getcwd())
    else:
        # Project/repo ref — try common default branch names
        for fallback in ["master", "main"]:
            ok, err = provider.checkout(fallback, os.getcwd())
            if ok:
                break
    if not ok:
        print(
            f"Warning: checkout failed: {err}",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )

# Sync with remote after checkout
subprocess.run(
    ["git", "pull", "--rebase", "--quiet"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)

# Record HEAD for the diff step
result = subprocess.run(
    ["git", "rev-parse", "HEAD"],
    capture_output=True,
    text=True,
    check=False,
)
head = result.stdout.strip() if result.returncode == 0 else ""
print(f"head_before={head}")
print("success=true")

head_before="{{ checkout.head_before }}"
if [ -z "$head_before" ]; then
  exit 0
fi
head_now=$(git rev-parse HEAD)
diff_dir="${SASE_TMPDIR:-${SASE_HOME:-$HOME/.sase}/tmp}/gh-diffs"
mkdir -p "$diff_dir"
diff_file=$(mktemp "$diff_dir/sase-gh-XXXXXX.diff")
if [ "$head_now" != "$head_before" ]; then
  # Commits were made — show only the last commit's diff
  git diff HEAD~1 HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  commit_msg=$(git log -1 --format='%s' HEAD)
  echo "meta_commit_message=$commit_msg"
else
  # No commits — show uncommitted changes
  git diff HEAD > "$diff_file" 2>/dev/null
  git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -z 2>/dev/null \
    | while IFS= read -r -d '' f; do
        git diff --no-index /dev/null "$f" 2>/dev/null
      done >> "$diff_file"
fi
if [ -s "$diff_file" ]; then
  echo "diff_path=$diff_file"
else
  rm -f "$diff_file"
fi

# Stash any uncommitted changes (including untracked files)
if ! git diff --quiet HEAD 2>/dev/null || [ -n "$(git ls-files --others --exclude-standard)" ]; then
  git stash push --include-untracked -m "gh-workflow-$(date +%s)" --quiet
  echo "stashed=true"
else
  echo "stashed=false"
fi
git fetch origin --quiet 2>&1 || true
git pull --rebase --quiet 2>/dev/null || true
echo "success=true"

from sase_github.scripts.gh_setup import main
main(
    gh_ref={{ gh_ref | tojson }},
    n={{ n | tojson }},
    release={{ release | tojson }},
    workflow_label={{ workflow_label | tojson }},
)

I’ll investigate the existing Bob reference system and Mac capture app, then compare implementation options and design the picker. I’ll use the SASE repository and memory skills to access the relevant material, and write an independent `__cdx.md` report without consulting the other researchers.


Bob already exposes reference types, reading state, titles, source links, and annotation counts through read-only commands. That makes a richer picker practical. Highlights’ FAQ says it is not scriptable, so I’m checking the macOS APIs for opening the original PDF directly in Highlights.


The main risk is building another filename browser. I recommend showing recognizable reference titles and types, with recent opens for quick return and relevance ranking once you type. I also found two gaps the design must handle: `bob ref list` defaults to the reading queue and caps results, while a PDF in `lib/` may have no indexed note yet.


I’m leaning toward a dedicated References panel inside the existing Mac app, with its own model and hotkey. That would reuse the panel and installation infrastructure while avoiding a second resident app. One detail needs care: the current hotkey manager handles a single shortcut, so a second action needs explicit routing to prevent both panels responding.


The report will specify the panel layout, keyboard behavior, metadata sources, and separate ordering rules for browsing and searching. I’ll also distinguish facts verified in code and documentation from proposed behavior, including macOS opening and focus handling that I could not test on this Linux host.


The design now includes a split panel with concise rows and richer details for the selected reference. The ordering rule is explicit: a blank query favors recent opens and ongoing reading; a typed query favors matches, with recent use only breaking ties. The report also covers unindexed PDFs, missing files, stale annotation counts, and validation before opening.


The report is written and registered as a durable snapshot. It recommends a modular References panel in the existing Mac app, backed by an explicit PDF catalog. I’m using the SASE finalization skill to preserve the report in the research repository.


Created the independent [research report](/home/bryan/.local/state/sase/workspaces/bobs-org/bob-cli/bob-cli_11/sase/repos/research/202610/highlights_reference_picker_native_panel_design__cdx.md) and registered its durable snapshot.

Recommendation: build a dedicated References panel inside the existing Mac app, with a Bob PDF catalog, relevance-based search, rich selected-reference details, and explicit opening in Highlights.
